segments: was mourning for him,
and he was very grieved over him.
And he commanded that his queen,
she whose name was Sorqoqtani Beki, the daughter of the brother of King John [Prester John],
should manage his realm.
Now she had four grown sons:
Möngke, who became Khan in the end,
and the second Kublai,
and the third Hulagu,
and the fourth Ariq Böke.
And she raised her sons so well in all of this,
that all the sons of kings were astonished at her conduct.
And she was a true and faithful Christian woman, like Helena.
And concerning her, a certain poet said:
"If I were to see another like her in the female sex,
I would say that the female sex is far superior to men."
And at that time Jochi died also,
the eldest son of Genghis Khan.
And he left seven grown sons, who are these:
Tamshal,
Orda,
Batu,
Shiban {OCR?: Sibaqan},
Tangqut,
Berke,
and Berkejar.
And from among these brothers, the Khan chose Batu,
and to him he committed the northern countries of the Slavs,
and the Alans,
and the Russians,
and the Bulgars.
And his dwelling was on the great river that is called Itil (the Volga?).
And this Batu, when he entered by the northern path from the land of the Iberians [Georgians] into the countries of the Bulgars and of the Scythians,
they destroyed their people with the edge of the sword,
and brought their kingdom to an end.
And because the command of the Khan went out thus:
that they should cut off and bring {OCR?: ܘܢܝܬܘܢ / ܘܢܛܫܘܢ?} the right ear of every slain man of the Bulgars and Russians,
when they counted the ears,
two hundred and seventy thousand ears were found with the Tatars.
And he gained strength further,
and prepared to enter even Constantinople from the region of the Bulgars; and the kings of the Franks heard and gathered together,
and they met with Batu,
and they broke him and put him to flight.
And no one of the Tatars entered again into the land of the Franks,
but they settled in that plain of the Qipchaqs.
Now the son of this Batu
was called Sartaq.
He loved the confession of the Christians and was baptized,
and learned to read books,
and was ordained a deacon.
He died, however, on the way when he was going to the service of Möngke Khan,
as it appears.
